subtitle: Generate passwords, pick a manager, add 2FA and keys.

subsections.title: Generate a Password
subsections.summary: A random password, made in your browser.

items.label: NordPass
items.desc: Zero-knowledge manager with breach scanning; closed source.

items.label: Proton Pass
items.desc: Open-source, end-to-end encrypted, with built-in email aliases.

items.label: PrivacyNotes
items.desc: Encrypted passwords alongside notes, tasks and files.

items.label: KeePassXC
items.desc: Free, open-source and offline — your vault is a file you control.

items.label: Bitwarden
items.desc: Open source, syncs everywhere, free for personal use.

items.label: 1Password
items.desc: Polished paid manager with a Secret Key on top of your password.

blocks.before: A password manager creates, stores and fills a unique password for every site. Pick one, then move your email and banking passwords into it first.

blocks.text: By device (recommended by Security in a Box)

items.label: KeePassXC
items.desc: Windows, macOS, Linux — free, open source, offline.

items.label: KeePassDX
items.desc: Android — opens the same vault file as KeePassXC.

items.label: Strongbox
items.desc: iPhone and Mac — opens KeePass vaults.

items.label: Bitwarden
items.desc: every device — syncs online, or self-host it.

subsections.title: 2FA & Authenticator Apps
subsections.summary: A second lock on your most important accounts.

blocks.html: Two-factor authentication asks for a second proof — usually a six-digit code from an app — on top of your password, so a stolen password alone isn’t enough. Prefer an app or security key over SMS codes, which can be stolen by SIM swapping. Store your backup codes in your password manager.

items.label: ente Auth
items.desc: Encrypted backup and sync of your codes across devices.

items.label: Aegis Authenticator
items.desc: Encrypted, open-source authenticator.

items.label: 2FAS
items.desc: Backups, sync and a browser extension for one-tap codes.

items.label: Tofu
items.desc: Simple open-source authenticator.

items.label: Proton Authenticator
items.desc: Free, open-source, on every platform.

items.label: Yubico Authenticator
items.desc: Keeps your codes on a YubiKey.

blocks.html: A hardware security key plugs into USB or taps your phone over NFC to prove it’s really you. Its secret never leaves the key, so a fake login page can’t steal it. Buy two — one to use, one kept safe as a backup.

items.label: Nitrokey
items.desc: Open-source keys, from FIDO2-only up to models with OpenPGP and TOTP.

items.label: YubiKey 5 Series
items.desc: Full-featured: FIDO2/passkeys, codes, smart card and OpenPGP.

items.label: Yubico Security Key
items.desc: Cheaper key for FIDO2 and passkeys only.

subsections.title: Bitcoin Wallets
subsections.summary: Keep crypto keys — and your history — private.

blocks.html: Bitcoin isn’t anonymous: every transaction is public and permanent, and one link to your identity can expose your whole history. A privacy-respecting, non-custodial wallet keeps the keys on your device. Treat its recovery phrase like your most important password — write it down offline and never type it into a website.

items.label: Cake Wallet
items.desc: Open-source wallet for Bitcoin and Monero; keys stay on your device.

items.label: Edge
items.desc: Easy mobile wallet with fingerprint unlock.

items.label: Electrum
items.desc: Long-running, lightweight desktop wallet.

items.label: Sparrow Wallet
items.desc: Desktop wallet with built-in CoinJoin for better privacy.

items.label: Wasabi
items.desc: Privacy-focused desktop wallet with CoinJoin.
